newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grain co-ops bid for United Grain Growers.
newsitem.headline: Canada grain co-ops bid for United Grain Growers.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on Thursday launched a C$172 million ($126 million) hostile takeover for United Grain Growers Ltd to block foreign bidders for Canada's third-largest grain handler.
United Grain's stock soared to record heights as investors speculated other bids may emerge to rival the C$13.75 ($10.11) per share offer from the two grain handing co-operatives.

"This acquisition will ensure that UGG's substantial assets are not acquired by foreign competitors and as such, it presents a defensive benefit for (Alberta Wheat Pool) and (Manitoba Pool)," said Alberta Wheat Pool Chief Financial Officer Geoff Southwood during a conference call.
Calgary-based Alberta Wheat Pool and Winnipeg-based Manitoba Pool Elevators are both farmer-owned grain handling co-operatives.
They already own 14.98 percent of United Grain's shares through a joint holding company which has an agreement to buy another 6.4 percent of United Grain's stock.
The offer requires the removal of a shareholder rights plan, or poison pill, which United Grain's board adopted last Friday. The bid is scheduled to expire on March 27.

"The board will need time to assess the adequacy and terms of the offer and we will make a statement when they've had time to do that," United Grain Chief Executive Officer Brian Hayward, said in a telephone interview.
The C$13.75-a-share offer represents a 34 percent premium to the average closing price of UGG's stock before the pools began buying shares in United Grain in January, Southwood said.
Investors speculated the company may be worth more.
United Grain's stock jumped C$1.75 to close at C$14.25 ($10.47) on the Toronto Stock Exchange, a 52-week high.
"If it is trading above the bid price it means people feel (United Grain's) value is not fully represented in the offer," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities in Toronto.
Commodity and equity analysts agreed nothing would prevent a rival bid from emerging.
"The pools are limited to what debt financing they can pick up. A U.S. company or any other company can come in because I don't see anything obstructing another bid coming in," one analyst said.
Rumours have persisted in the past year that Nebraska-based ConAgra Inc. or Illinois-based Archer Daniels Midland Co. were interested in buying United Grain.
Officials at both firms were unavailable for comment on Thursday.

United Grain is Canada's third-largest grain handler after Saskatchewan Wheat Pool and Alberta Wheat Pool. UGG operates 173 elevator facilities in Western Canada, two terminals in Thunder Bay, Ontario and one in Vancouver, British Columbia.
United Grain also owns a 16.3 percent interest in a terminal in Prince Rupert, British Columbia.

United Grain made history in 1992 when it became the first Canadian grain co-operative to offer shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Saskatchewan Wheat Pool followed its rival onto Canada's largest stock market last year.

Dominion Bond Rating Service on Thursday placed all three grain handling companies under review with negative implications, citing concerns that any acquisition would be entirely financed through debt.
